sampling.request_order: six forward rotations then six reverse rotations; each identity twice at every position per policy
sampling.shared_session_scope: created inside batch; destroyed before batch timer stop; never retained across batches
sampling.fresh_session_scope: created and destroyed for each request within batch
sampling.timer: std::chrono::steady_clock, native milliseconds; total includes creation/setup/compile/diagnostic capture/destruction/endpoint cleanup; JSON serialization and pre/post batch RSS sampling outside timer
sampling.process_scope: one serial process; process loading/exit outside batch metric; process caches persist across batches; process duration separately recorded

acceptance.parent_review: Independent batch/per-cell statistics, balanced positions, lifecycle boundaries/counters, 168 PTX hashes and referenced artifact hashes verified. No production-runner speedup or material runtime claim.

memory.measurement: Linux /proc/self/statm RSS checkpoints and getrusage process cumulative high-water RSS; no per-batch peak isolation
memory.interpretation: Post-release RSS retains allocator/library caches; equal policy-boundary RSS and bounded plateau do not establish an unbounded leak or a universal leak-free guarantee. Every session/request handle released within each batch. No forced allocator trim or cache clearing. Creation/release counters establish explicit API handle operations and null endpoints, not destruction of every internal object.

inherited_runtime_preservation.failure_ledger: runtime-validation.slice-210.json: unresolved_failures and resolved_failure_history; all histories retained

limitations: Single host/build/material and one bounded six-cell API sequence; no production-runner speedup claimed.
Process startup, independent ptxas assembly, kernel dispatch and application runtime are outside batch metric.
Only finite 28-batch memory observation; allocator retention is not automatically a leak.
Ordinary host services remain running; no competing builds or benchmarks.
No production runner, timeout recovery or crash isolation implemented.
No material binding/input/output oracle is available; no kernel correctness or speed claim.

proposed_next_slice.scope: Opt-in maximum-six-cell API worker for complex corpus only; fresh-process lane remains mandatory.
requirements: Supervise per-cell deadlines and isolate crashes to bounded batch processes.
Preserve failed active cells, incomplete suffixes and separately recorded recovery attempts; never mask failure as pass.
Preserve exact cell identity/options and target/entry/hash/assembly oracles.
Use fresh requests, new global each batch, exit worker at endpoint, no material-module/IR cache.
Measure full process startup/exit and timeout/crash handling before asserting runner speedup.
Retain per-cell timing deltas rather than accumulated global profiler totals.
Require full frozen/discovery checkpoint and all six complex cells after final production changes.
